name: Founder decision: Name the room designation, and read the door as the threshold's holder
text_content:
P25 and P5, founder-gated. Brandon's ruling puts the room in one seat, and a seat cannot be in the building for every service of every open period. The record's own device for accountability in the moment is the per-service functional designation (WP p.10). The team recommends a room designation named at the brief, defaulting to the Maitre d on every service the Maitre d works and otherwise a named floor seat with a complete readiness form and range card and no non-negotiable line, holding the room's live functions (coverage, pattern recognition, backing up without intercepting, the server's above-threshold destination, the transition trigger, emergency authority for the room) and nothing else the seat holds. Alongside it, the team recommends reading canon's "Maître d' at the top of the porch steps" as a register set by whoever holds the door that service, with the Maitre d at the steps when free, rather than a fixed post, because a room owner walking every table is a room no one is reading; that reading routes to canon's owner. Neither is a second seat. Blocks every brief from the first training service and readiness rows 95, 96, and 106. Urgent.

Filed by Session 8 of the Scaling People translation program. Session task 86ajgmhxx. Reasoning lives on the S8 page of the Sŏn Operating System doc 2ky45bmy-17253.
